title: Devagiri Pays for a Throne
subtitle: How Devagiri’s hidden gold bought the throne of Delhi
moral: Treasure can become a throne before it becomes a state.

sources.note: Delhi court tradition with detailed account of Alauddin's rise.
Contemporary Khalji panegyric for the campaigns.
Modern source-critical political and military history.

panels.shot: split-panel wide, half showing Alauddin atop a northern rampart with Delhi behind him, half showing Ramachandra on Devagiri’s hill-fort above the Deccan plain

dialogue.text: In 1296, a hidden road of gold runs from Devagiri’s hill-fort to Delhi’s throne—Alauddin Khalji and Ramachandra Yadava will both ride it, but only one will reach a crown.

panels.shot: medium close-up on Alauddin in a dim Delhi hall, half-lit, as an elder Jalaluddin sits in the background blurred

dialogue.text: Barani tells of a restless nephew in Delhi—Alauddin, governor of Kara—watching his uncle Sultan Jalaluddin grow cautious as the treasury thins and frontier foes press.

panels.shot: over-the-shoulder shot from behind Alauddin, looking at a map spread on a low carpet, north and south marked with pebbles

dialogue.text: The chronicles say he dreams not of border raids but of a throne, and knows a fact every Delhi commander whispers—without new treasure, ambition is only dust.

panels.shot: wide establishing shot of Devagiri hill-fort dominating the landscape, with Ramachandra in the foreground

dialogue.text: Far to the south, Ramachandra of the Yadavas rules from Devagiri, a hill-fort rich with trade and tribute; the Deccan’s wealth gathers under his walls, though no Yadava chronicle survives to sing his side.

panels.shot: medium shot of Alauddin before Jalaluddin in a tented camp, banners fluttering, soldiers beyond

dialogue.speaker: alauddin_khalji_and_ramachandra_yadava
dialogue.text: “Let me raid the south, uncle—beyond the Narmada lies easy plunder.”

panels.shot: close-up on Jalaluddin’s thoughtful face, Alauddin blurred behind, soldiers outside

dialogue.text: Barani records that Jalaluddin, mild and trusting, grants his nephew men and leave to raid—never guessing that Kara’s governor weighs more than coin in his plans.

panels.shot: long tracking wide shot of a column of horsemen crossing a river at dusk, silhouettes against the sky

dialogue.text: So begins the secret ride. Khusrau and Barani agree—Alauddin slips from the north with a small, chosen force, heading for Devagiri without openly naming his true target.

panels.shot: overhead wide shot of the column moving through scrubland and rocky outcrops of the Deccan fringe

dialogue.text: Day after day they ride, avoiding great towns and main roads. Modern historians note the boldness of the march—deep into the Deccan with no supply line, gambling on surprise.

panels.shot: first glimpse wide shot of Devagiri from the raiders’ perspective, partly obscured by trees

dialogue.text: At last the hill of Devagiri rises before them. The chroniclers say the lower city below the fort swarms with traders and storehouses—rich, but poorly guarded against a northern storm.

panels.shot: chaotic wide shot of Delhi horsemen pouring into the lower city streets, citizens fleeing

dialogue.text: Barani speaks of a swift strike on the town below. Delhi horsemen crash into the lower city, seizing stores and wealth, before Ramachandra can fully draw his strength up into the fort.

panels.shot: medium shot of captives—Brahmins, merchants, townsfolk—herded together under guard

dialogue.text: Barani’s pen does not look away. He notes prisoners taken—Brahmins and merchants among them—and some put to death during the siege, the cost of Alauddin’s hunger written in human lives.

panels.shot: dramatic low-angle shot of Ramachandra at the fort gate, rallying soldiers, arrows ready

dialogue.speaker: alauddin_khalji_and_ramachandra_yadava
dialogue.text: “Hold the heights! Let the hill be our shield!”

panels.shot: wide siege shot of Delhi forces attempting to press up the slope under missiles

dialogue.text: The hill itself fights for Ramachandra. Devagiri’s steep ways and strong walls slow Alauddin, and the chronicles hint at hard presses and reverses before negotiation opens a different path.

panels.shot: tense medium shot inside a hall on the fort, Alauddin and Ramachandra seated opposite, guards behind

dialogue.text: Barani and later Isami agree—the siege ends not with a stormed gate, but with submission. Ramachandra yields treasure and acknowledges the Sultan of Delhi, and Alauddin gains what he truly came for.

panels.shot: medium close-up of Ramachandra’s face, conflicted, as chests are carried past behind him

dialogue.text: We do not have Ramachandra’s own words. No Yadava chronicle survives. But the scene is clear in Delhi’s record—a southern king paying heavily to spare his capital and kingdom.

panels.shot: wide shot of pack animals laden with chests and bundles leaving Devagiri, Alauddin overseeing

dialogue.text: Khusrau praises the haul without numbers; Barani links it directly to what comes next. Alauddin does not linger to annex Devagiri. He rides north, his carts heavier than when he came.

panels.shot: dark, intimate shot of Alauddin at night, counting and inspecting jewels and coins by lamplight

dialogue.text: Under canvas and in guarded rooms, the treasure is weighed and sorted. Modern historians see here the crucial hinge—Devagiri’s wealth turning from southern hoard to northern war-chest.

panels.shot: wide shot of Alauddin meeting Jalaluddin on a riverbank near Kara, greeting warmly, soldiers in background

dialogue.text: When the Devagiri loot is safe, Barani says, Alauddin invites Jalaluddin to Kara with promises of loyalty. The newfound wealth pays wages, buys blades, and gives his camp the glitter of power.

panels.shot: low-angle shot of Alauddin later on the Delhi throne, regally seated, Ramachandra shown in inset background paying homage

dialogue.text: Soon after, Jalaluddin is dead by his nephew’s hand and Alauddin is Sultan. From then, sources speak of Devagiri’s ruler sending tribute—Delhi’s shadow stretching further into the Deccan.

panels.shot: wide reflective shot of Devagiri hill-fort at sunset, half in light, half in shadow

dialogue.text: Barani, Khusrau and later Jackson all trace the line—one daring raid, no conquest yet, but a river of wealth that topples a Sultan, feeds an empire, and binds the Deccan to Delhi’s story ever after.
